# AlphaAgents: Large Language Model based Multi-Agents for Equity Portfolio Constructions

| Field | Gloss | Quote from the paper |
|---|---|---|
| **task** | Using role-based LLM multi-agent collaboration and debate to support stock selection in equity research and portfolio management under different risk tolerances. | “This study investigates the application of role-based multi-agent systems to support stock selection in equity research and portfolio management.” |
| **architecture** | Three specialist agents (Fundamental with 10-K/yfinance pull and RAG tools, Sentiment with news summarization tool, Valuation with volatility/return tool) coordinated by an AutoGen group chat assistant; round-robin debate until consensus; risk profiles set via prompts. | “We utilize the Microsoft AutoGen framework (Wu et al., 2023) as the infrastructure for our multi-agent system, leveraging its group chat and assistant agent capabilities.” |
| **data** | 10-K and 10-Q disclosures, Bloomberg financial news, and Yahoo Finance historical price and volume data; universe of 15 randomly selected technology-sector stocks. | “The primary data sources utilized in the system are listed in Table 1, including 10-K and 10-Q financial disclosures, Bloomberg financial news, and historical stock price and volume data from Yahoo Finance.” |
| **window** | Agents used data and news from January 2024; portfolios initialized February 1, 2024 and monitored over the following four months. | “The agents were trained using data and news from January 2024. Based on each agent’s responses and their final decisions following debate and collaboration, we constructed the corresponding portfolios: the valuation agent portfolio, news sentiment agent portfolio, fundamental agent portfolio, and the final multi-agent portfolio, all initialized on February 1, 2024.” |
| **models** | GPT4o as the LLM; GPT 4-o also cited as embedding model in the RAG tool. | “After experimenting with various GPT models, we chose GPT4o as the model for our experiments.” |
| **baselines** | Equal-weighted benchmark portfolio of the 15 tech stocks, and single-agent portfolios from the fundamental and valuation agents. | “For comparison, single-agent portfolios from the fundamental and valuation agents were also created; the sentiment agent was excluded due to insufficient news coverage in some cases.” |
| **headline_result** | Qualitative only: in the risk-neutral setting the multi-agent portfolio outperformed the benchmark and single-agent portfolios over the test window; in the risk-averse setting all agent portfolios underperformed the benchmark. | “In the risk-neutral setting, the proposed multi-agent outperforms the benchmark as well as the single agent framework during the testing window.” |
